name: Non-Immigrant O Visa (Thai Spouse or Family) and 1-Year Marriage Extension
summary: For people married to a Thai citizen or with Thai children. You enter on a 90-day Non-Immigrant O visa, then extend to 1 year at a Thai immigration office by showing 400,000 THB in a Thai bank or 40,000 THB a month in income, plus your marriage and family documents. You may work, but only with a work permit.
seoTitle: Thai Marriage Visa (Non-O): 400,000 THB Rule and 1-Year Extension
seoDescription: How the Non-Immigrant O visa for Thai spouses and parents of Thai children works: 400,000 THB or 40,000 THB a month, the home visit, documents and fees.
validity: The visa is valid for 3 months for a single entry and gives you up to 90 days in Thailand. A marriage or family extension then gives you up to 1 year at a time.
extendableDetail: Yes. Before your 90 days end, apply at your local immigration office for a 1-year extension based on marriage to a Thai citizen or supporting a Thai child (form TM7, fee 1,900 THB). You can renew every year.
feeNote: 2,000 THB on the Thai fee schedule for a single entry, charged in local currency by embassies. Each 1-year extension costs 1,900 THB.
financialRequirement: At least 400,000 THB in a bank account or a monthly income of at least 40,000 THB. For the 1-year extension the savings must be in a Thai bank account in your name, usually for 2 months before you apply.
processingTime: Processing for the visa depends on the embassy. Marriage extensions often take longer than other extensions: you may get a 30-day "under consideration" stamp while officers check your marriage, sometimes with a home visit.
keyRequirements: You are legally married to a Thai citizen, or you are the parent of a Thai child.
You have 400,000 THB in savings or 40,000 THB a month in income.
Your marriage is registered in Thailand (Kor Ror 2), or a foreign marriage is certified and registered at a Thai district office (Kor Ror 22).
You and your spouse or child live together at the address you give immigration.
You need a work permit before you start any job.
documents: Passport valid for at least 6 months
Recent passport-style photo (taken within the last 6 months)
Bank statements for the last 3 months showing at least 400,000 THB, or proof of 40,000 THB monthly income
Marriage certificate, or your child's birth certificate
Your Thai spouse's ID card and house registration book (tabien baan)
For the extension: form TM7, 4x6 cm photos and copies of your passport pages
For the extension: a letter from your Thai bank confirming the balance, plus your bank book
For the extension: a map to your home and family photos taken together at the house
Birth certificates of your children, if you have any

howToApply.detail: If you married abroad, have the certificate translated and certified, then register it at a Thai district office (amphur) to get a Kor Ror 22.
Apply on thaievisa.go.th under "To stay with Thai family". Upload proof of funds, your spouse's ID and proof of your relationship.
Fill in the free TDAC in the 3 days before you arrive. You get up to 90 days.
Keep at least 400,000 THB in a Thai account in your name for the required period, or get proof of 40,000 THB monthly income.
Go to the immigration office with your Thai spouse, both sets of documents, photos and 1,900 THB. Officers may interview you both.
You may get a 30-day "under consideration" stamp and a home visit. Return on the date given to collect the full 1-year extension.

bestFor: People married to a Thai citizen
Spouses who want to work in Thailand later with a work permit
Anyone for whom 400,000 THB is easier than the 800,000 THB retirement route
notFor: Couples who aren't legally married (the relationship must be registered)
Families of non-Thai residents (there's a separate Non-O category for that)
Anyone expecting to work without a work permit
commonMistakes: Not registering a foreign marriage in Thailand before the extension
Going to the extension appointment without your Thai spouse
Too few family photos, or photos that don't show your home
Starting a job before the work permit is issued
Leaving Thailand without a re-entry permit

faqs.q: How much money do I need?
faqs.a: At least 400,000 THB in savings or 40,000 THB a month in income. For the extension, the savings must be in a Thai bank account in your name.

faqs.q: Can I work on this visa?
faqs.a: Yes, but only after you get a work permit. The marriage extension lets you live in Thailand, and a Thai employer can then apply for your work permit.

faqs.q: Does my Thai spouse need to come to the immigration office?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Offices normally want to see both of you and may interview you together.
They might. Officers can check that you live together at the address you gave. Keep a map and photos of your home ready.

faqs.q: Can I use this if we married abroad?
faqs.a: Yes, once the marriage is registered at a Thai district office. You then get a Kor Ror 22 to show immigration.
The extension is based on the marriage. If it ends, you need to switch to another visa or leave. Ask your immigration office about your options.

faqs.q: Can I extend based on my Thai child instead?
faqs.a: Yes. Parents who support a Thai child can extend on that basis, with the child's birth certificate and proof of funds.
